subject: Renewal: support scaling and premium SLA options
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@vantagepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: support scaling and premium SLA options

Hi Erin,

Hope you're well — as we head into VantagePay's renewal window (Dec 1), I wanted to lay out a clear path for a support and SLA refresh that matches the usage growth you signaled on the Q3 call. High level: you asked for tighter latency SLOs, a dedicated reserve for predictable throughput spikes, and a smoother on-call/ops handoff during peak events.

Attached is a short options summary and a preliminary quote for a Premium SLA add-on that includes: 
- 99.9% uptime SLA with a 50ms p50 latency target on our dedicated inference variant
- Reserved burst capacity pool (up to 25% above baseline commit)
- 24/7 priority support with a named on-call escalation path and monthly runbook reviews

If this aligns, we can propose a mutual action plan with milestones for contract signature, ops onboarding, and a dry-run failover test before the renewal effective date. I copied Marissa for the onboarding notes and Ben for commercial sign-off.

Two quick asks:
1) Can legal at VantagePay share any non-negotiable contract items now so we can incorporate them into the draft?
2) Do you have a preferred billing cadence for committed capacity (monthly vs. quarterly)?

Happy to run through the numbers live — I have availability next week Tuesday/Wednesday afternoon PT.

Best,

Lauren Bishop
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Attachment: VP-SLA-quote-20281109.pdf (PDF, 48KB)
From: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@vantagepay.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: VantagePay Legal <contracts@vantagepay.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Oct 2028 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: support scaling and premium SLA options

Hi Lauren — thanks for the summary and the quick turnaround. A few follow-ups from our side:

- On latency: we'd like the SLA to reference p95 tail latency rather than p50 for external customer-facing flows. Can the premium SLA be scoped to p95 <= 120ms for our production endpoint?
- On reserved capacity: we operate heavy payroll windows the first three business days of each month. Can the reserved pool be guaranteed for that cadence?
- Billing: we prefer monthly invoicing for committed capacity but would consider quarterly if there's a material discount.

Finally, legal has asked for an initial draft contract or term sheet to review redlines early. I'm CCing our contracts alias — they'll upload a short redline checklist if there are must-have constraints.

Can you put a short mutual action plan in a spreadsheet with owners and dates? That helps our procurement.

Thanks — available Thu morning PT for a quick call.

Erin
VP Strategic Ops
VantagePay
Attachment: (none)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@vantagepay.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Oct 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: support scaling and premium SLA options

Hi Erin — looping in operations details here.

We can absolutely scope the SLA to a p95 <= 120ms for the production endpoint. A few operational notes:
- Reserved capacity: we can reserve a monthly burst pool that is active on the first three business days. We'll configure autoscaling thresholds so that reserved capacity is consumed before spilling into on-demand.
- Dry-run: recommended a staged failover test two weeks post-signature; ops runbook will include step-by-step escalation and rollback.
- On-call: named engineer escalation (tier 2) is included in Premium SLA; for guaranteed response windows we'll provide an on-call roster.

I've attached the mutual action plan (spreadsheet) with proposed dates and owners, plus the draft quote Lauren mentioned. Please review and suggest edits to dates/owners.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Attachments: VantagePay-MAP-20281109.csv (CSV, 4KB); VP-SLA-quote-20281109.pdf (PDF, 48KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@vantagepay.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Nov 2028 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: support scaling and premium SLA options

Erin — quick note from the revenue side. I'm comfortable approving a one-time 3% concession on the committed capacity line if VantagePay signs by Nov 20 and agrees to monthly billing. That concession is intended to cover the ramping risk for the added reserved pool.

Karthik, please confirm the on-call escalation SLAs are compatible with the pricing band we discussed.

Lauren — if Erin agrees, can you get procurement and contracts working toward a November signature? We'll hold the concession until COB Nov 20.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Hi legal — please find the vendor-side redline attached. Key asks for Redwood before we route for signature:
1) Termination: allow VantagePay 60 days termination for convenience rather than 30.
2) Data retention: request logs and audit trails retained for 180 days; we also need a documented process for ad-hoc compliance exports.
3) Liability cap: propose a cap at 6 months of committed fees.
4) Audit access: limited audit rights for SOC-type reviews with appropriate NDA.

Please see attached redline (VP-Contract-Redline.docx).

--
VantagePay Legal (contracts@vantagepay.com)
